course_description:
This course will help you learn the basic fundamentals of digital health technology through hands-on experience, and through exposure to the real-world use of data and informatics in the health industry. The course includes a MOOC component that provides a broad introduction to healthcare informatics. There will also be a number of guest lecturers from industry talking about the current digital health landscape. A major part of the course is composed of a group software development project building a FHIR app for use in a clinical (or clinical education) setting, with real-world clients. FHIR (Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources) is the new standard for sharing health data that is revolutionising how clinicians and patients are interacting with digital technology and has been adopted by major global IT companies (e.g., Apple, Google, Microsoft, etc.) and digital health vendors (e.g., Cerner, EPIC, etc.). Be at the forefront of healthcare application development by learning about and developing new FHIR and SMART-on-FHIR applications.

COMP3820 introduces students to interoperability standards for exchanging electronic healthcare data via the FHIR technical standard.

AI Use in this Course

AI tools may be used to support learning and task completion in this course, and the course provides guidance on appropriate use; their use will be expected in some aspects of the course, such as the creation of synthetic patient data. Students are expected to apply their own judgement when using these tools, to check outputs carefully, and to ensure that all submitted work reflects their own understanding. Students are responsible for ensuring that any use of AI complies with academic integrity requirements and is appropriately acknowledged.

learning_outcomes.description: Analyse and explain key aspects of the digital health landscape.
Apply the Software Development Life Cycle and human-centred design principles to design, develop, and document a functional digital health application using FHIR and interoperability standards.
Analyse and address user experience challenges in the design and development of a digital health application.
Communicate effectively with stakeholders to gather requirements and manage expectations over the course of the project.
Demonstrate an ability to collaborate effectively within a team to achieve shared project goals, while managing individual responsibilities.
Evaluate and justify software development processes and design decisions within the context of building digital health applications.

assessment_details.task_description: In teams, you will develop a functional SMART-on-FHIR digital healthcare application. The project will be supported and monitored through a series of formative in-class milestones. All team members must attend these sessions, and you will be expected to discuss your progress and demonstrate your individual contributions. These milestones include: Part A: Proposal and Requirements (Week 4): Define the healthcare problem, users, requirements, and relevant FHIR resources. Part B: Design and Architecture (Week 7): Present the system architecture, data flows, interface design, and interoperability approach. Part C: Prototype (Week 10): Demonstrate a functional prototype implementing core SMART-on-FHIR features. Assessment focuses on problem definition, application of FHIR and interoperability concepts, technical design, implementation quality, and the suitability of the solution for its healthcare context. This task has been designed to be challenging, authentic and complex. Whilst students may use AI and/or MT technologies, successful completion of assessment in this course will require students to critically engage in specific contexts and tasks for which artificial intelligence will provide only limited support and guidance. A failure to reference generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. Read full task description Hide full task description

The focus is not on memorising information, but on understanding, applying judgement, and demonstrating your own thinking.
assessment_details.submission_guidelines:
Submission for each component includes:
Team Charter: One team submission via Blackboard by the specified deadline (template provided in class). Team Final Report: One team submission via Turnitin on Blackboard by the specified deadline. Team Final Codebase and Team Project Video: One team submission of each item via Blackboard by the specified deadline.
For team submissions, only one team member is required to submit on behalf of the group.
Deferral or extension
You cannot defer or apply for an extension for this assessment.
Additionally, this course uses team-based assessment where the team assignment is developed and iterated on with students needing to act on regular formative feedback over the semester. Extensions for groupwork are typically not available as this impacts on all members of the team. However, if a group encounters extraordinary difficulties in meeting a deadline, they should contact the Course Coordinator in advance of the due date. Groups will be asked to meet with the Course Coordinator, and be prepared to submit their work, as it stands.
Late submission
A penalty of 1 grade for each 24 hour period from time submission is due will apply for up to 7 days. After 7 days you will receive a mark of 0.

learning_activities.topic: Guest Speakers Guest talks from industry will occur within some of the studio sessions, depending on speaker availability.
Online Course Delivered via the "Digital Health on FHIR" online course covering the key concepts of digital health.

Weekly Studio Sessions Students will work with each other on their team project and related activities that support the assessment deliverables. Studio sessions will be delivered in-person (face-to-face) and so you will be expected to participate in an entirely in-person capacity in the sessions. By default, these sessions will not be recorded. Progress on the team project will be monitored during these sessions and students will have an opportunity to receive feedback prior to Census (Week 6). This course relies on students undertaking a self-directed team-based and individual learning approach towards the achievement of assessment deliverables. Active student participation is expected at all sessions . Students are expected to meaningfully contribute to all aspects of the team project. The teaching team are available to assist with issues.
